_what: Paired significance for the frontier-model comparison. Every system sees the same 192 drawings, so McNemar (exact binomial, conditioning on discordant pairs) and a paired bootstrap over circuits are the right tests.

claude_A.sentence: pipeline vs claude_A: 84 circuits only pipeline solves, 6 only claude_A, 18 both, 84 neither. exact McNemar p = 1.081e-18 -> distinguishable at alpha=0.05.

gpt_A.sentence: pipeline vs gpt_A: 81 circuits only pipeline solves, 3 only gpt_A, 21 both, 87 neither. exact McNemar p = 1.022e-20 -> distinguishable at alpha=0.05.

claude_B.sentence: pipeline vs claude_B: 23 circuits only pipeline solves, 27 only claude_B, 79 both, 63 neither. exact McNemar p = 0.6718 -> NOT distinguishable at alpha=0.05.

gpt_B.sentence: pipeline vs gpt_B: 11 circuits only pipeline solves, 40 only gpt_B, 91 both, 50 neither. exact McNemar p = 5.704e-05 -> distinguishable at alpha=0.05.

the_assisted_frontier_question.question: Is the assisted frontier result (Claude, variant B, 0.5295 +/- 0.0167) distinguishable from the pipeline (0.5312, seed 0)?
the_assisted_frontier_question.answer: NO -- not distinguishable. The paired difference is -0.0208 with 95% CI [-0.0938, +0.0521], which contains zero, and exact McNemar gives p = 0.672. The manuscript must not describe either system as ahead of the other on the assisted task.
